svg.title: Torque on a door seen from above
svg.desc: Six overhead views of a door hinged on the left and opened 25° from the wall. (a) A force F pushes perpendicular to the door at distance r from the hinge, so r = r⊥ and the torque is counterclockwise. (b) A smaller force F′ at the same point gives a smaller counterclockwise torque. (c) The same force at a smaller distance r′ = r′⊥ gives a smaller counterclockwise torque. (d) The force −F, opposite to (a), gives a clockwise torque. (e) A horizontal force of the same magnitude at the same point makes angle θ with the door; the perpendicular distance from the hinge to its line of action is r⊥ = r sin θ, so the counterclockwise torque is smaller. (f) A force pulling straight along the door away from the hinge has θ = 0° and r⊥ = 0, so it produces no torque.
